The jar mix should account for the dry ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 tablespoons baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1/2 cup flaked coconut, plus the layered add-ins such as 3/4 cup chopped pecans and 2 cups packed brown sugar if your jar was assembled that way.
I see the coconut and brown sugar layers. Should I sift anything, or just dump it all in?
Empty the whole jar of brownie mix into a large mixing bowl. Don't worry about sifting; just stir through the dry mixture to loosen the brown sugar and break up any lumps.
The brown sugar had a few clumps, but I broke them down with a spoon. What wet ingredients go in?
Add 3/4 cup softened butter, 2 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract to the bowl.
The butter is soft but not melted. Is that okay for mixing?
Yes, softened butter is right here. Mix everything until the batter looks evenly combined, with no dry floury pockets at the bottom of the bowl.
It's thick and sticky now. Do I need to thin it out before putting it in the pan?
No need to thin it. Scrape the thick batter into the greased 9x13 inch pan and spread it as evenly as you can, pushing it into the corners.
The top is mostly level, though the coconut makes it look a little bumpy. How long should it bake?
Bake it at 375 degrees F for 25 minutes. Set a timer, and keep the pan centered in the oven for even baking.
Timer is set. When it comes out, what should I look for before cutting?
Let the brownies cool in the pan before slicing. The surface should look set, the edges should hold their shape, and the center should not look loose or wet.
Can you walk me through Broccoli Chicken Roli while I get everything ready and into the oven?
Absolutely. Start by clearing space for a large mixing bowl and a foil-lined cookie sheet. You'll also want the oven available, since it needs to preheat to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C.
I'm at the counter with the bowl out. Which chopped ingredients should go in first?
Add the main vegetables and chicken to the large bowl: 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat, 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli, 1/2 cup chopped onion, and 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper.
The chicken, broccoli, onion, and green pepper are in the bowl. The mixture looks pretty bulky.

That's fine for this stage. The recipe has you combine those with cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic in the same large bowl, so leave enough room to fold everything together without spilling.
I've added the cheese, mayo, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic. Should I stir gently or really work it together?

Mix it all together until the chicken and broccoli are evenly coated and the onion and bell pepper are spread through the filling. Use a folding motion if the bowl is full, then scrape the sides so the seasonings don't sit in one spot.
It's mixed, but I haven't turned on the oven yet. Is this when I heat it?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C. While it heats, cover a cookie sheet with aluminum foil so it's ready when you need it.
The foil is on the cookie sheet. Should the shiny side matter here?
Either side is fine for lining the cookie sheet. Smooth the foil down so the surface is stable and any edges don't catch when you move the food onto it.
The filling is sitting in the bowl while the oven heats. Is there anything I should fix before moving on?

Give the mixture one last stir from the bottom of the bowl. Look for pockets of plain mayonnaise, mustard, or seasoning, and make sure the chopped chicken, broccoli, onion, and green bell pepper are evenly distributed.
The oven is nearly ready. How should I handle serving once it's cooked?

Keep the foil-lined cookie sheet steady when transferring, and let the finished Broccoli Chicken Roli settle briefly before serving so the filling holds together better. Check that the texture looks evenly mixed and the hot filling is safe to handle before plating.
I'm making Black Bean Lasagna Rolls tonight. Can you walk me through getting set up before I start cooking?
Absolutely. Put a large pot of water on for the 8 lasagna noodles, and set out a colander, mixing bowl, spoon or spatula, and a baking dish or work surface for assembling the rolls.
While the water heats, what ingredients should be on the counter?

Measure 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese, open the 1 (15 ounce) container of part-skim ricotta cheese, and drain the 1 (4.5 ounce) can of chopped green chiles. You'll also need 1/2 teaspoon chili powder for the filling.
The water is close to boiling. Should I salt it or add oil for the noodles?
Cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions, but omit salt and fat. When they're done, drain them well so the filling won't slide around.
The noodles are cooking. Can I make the cheese mixture now?
Yes. In the bowl, combine the ricotta, Monterey Jack, drained green chiles, chili powder, and the remaining filling ingredients called for with the cheeses. Stir until it looks evenly mixed.
The noodles are drained and a little slippery. How should I lay them out?
Lay the noodles flat in a single layer if you can, with enough space to spread filling on one side of each noodle. If they stick, separate them gently so they don't tear.
How much of the cheese filling goes on each noodle?
Divide the cheese mixture evenly among the noodles, then spread it over one side of each noodle from end to end, leaving just a little margin so it doesn't squeeze out too much when rolled.
I've got the filling spread. Where do the black beans go?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on each noodle. Try to distribute them so every roll has a similar amount and will roll up neatly.
What's the cleanest way to roll them without losing the filling?

Roll each noodle up jellyroll-style, beginning at the narrow end. Place the rolls seam-side down so they hold their shape, then check that the filling is contained and the rolls are ready for serving or the next recipe step.
Can you walk me through Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats while I get the oven and toppings ready?
Absolutely. Heat the oven to 375 degrees F, and make sure you have 4 medium baked potatoes that are already cooked and ready to quarter lengthwise.
The potatoes are baked. Should I cut them before measuring the ranch and cheese?
Yes. Quarter the potatoes lengthwise first so they look like sturdy wedges. Then set out 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing and 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese.
I've got the ranch and Cheddar on the counter. Do I need the green onions right now?
Only if you want them as a topping. Slice the green onions and keep them nearby, but the potato skins, Ranch, and Cheddar are the main parts to build before baking.
The potato quarters are on my board. How much potato should I scoop out?
Scoop out the flesh from each skin carefully, leaving enough potato attached so the skins hold their boat shape and do not tear.
Some of the skins feel thin. What should I do with the Ranch?
Brush or spoon the Ranch inside the potato skins rather than pressing hard. A light coating across the inside is enough.
The insides are coated, and the scooped potato is still warm. Does it go back in now?
Yes, place the potato back into the skins. Keep each one level on the baking pan so the filling stays put.
They're filled and sitting on the pan. How should I add the cheese?
Sprinkle the shredded Cheddar over the filled potato boats, covering the tops evenly so it melts across the surface.
They're ready for the oven. How long should I bake them?
Bake them at 375 degrees F for 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted. Add the optional sliced green onions after baking if you want a fresh finish.
I'm making Eggnog II and have a saucepan, whisk, and metal spoon out. Can you walk me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also want a larger bowl or sink ready with ice water for cooling the pan quickly later.
The eggs are beaten in a bowl. Should I pour everything into the saucepan before turning on the burner?
Yes. In the large saucepan, combine the beaten eggs, the milk, and the 1/3 cup sugar before heating. Stir them together well so the sugar starts dissolving and the eggs are evenly mixed in.
It's mixed and the pan is on the stove. What heat should I use so the eggs don't scramble?
Use medium heat and keep stirring steadily. The goal is a smooth custard-like mixture, so don't let it sit still on the bottom of the pan.
I'm stirring with a spoon and whisk nearby. How do I know when it's thick enough?
Dip the metal spoon into the mixture. It's ready to come off the heat when the eggnog coats the spoon instead of running off immediately in a thin stream.
It's starting to coat the spoon, but I'm worried about leaving it on too long.
Once it clearly coats the metal spoon, remove the saucepan from the heat right away. That keeps the eggs from overcooking.
The pan is off the burner. I have a bowl of ice water in the sink—do I set the saucepan in it?
Yes, place the pan in the sink or bowl of ice water carefully so water doesn't splash into the eggnog. Stir the mixture while it cools quickly for 1 to 2 minutes.
It has cooled for about 2 minutes and looks smoother. Where does the vanilla fit in?
Stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract now, while the mixture is off the heat. Mix gently until it's evenly blended.
Before I serve it, anything I should look over?

Make sure the texture is smooth, the vanilla is mixed through, and the eggnog has cooled from the quick ice-water stir. If it coated the spoon before you removed it from the heat, you followed the key cooking cue.
Can you walk me through Eclairs II from setup through the stovetop dough? I want to keep the counter organized.
Absolutely. Heat the oven to 450 degrees F, or 230 degrees C, and grease a cookie sheet so it's ready before the dough gets hot.
Oven is heating and the cookie sheet is greased. What ingredients should I measure before turning on the burner?
Measure 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water for the saucepan. Also have 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt ready together, since those go in after the butter-water mixture boils.
I've got the butter, water, flour, and salt measured. Should anything else be nearby for later?
If you're continuing with the fuller éclair assembly, keep 4 eggs and a 1 (5 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix within reach, but don't add them to the saucepan at this stage.
Got it. The saucepan is on the stove. Do I add the butter and water cold, or wait for the pan to warm?
Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to a medium saucepan together, then put it over heat. Stir as it warms so the butter melts evenly.
The butter is starting to melt, and the water is steaming. What am I watching for before adding the dry ingredients?
Bring it to a full boil while stirring, and make sure the butter has melted completely. You want one hot, blended mixture before the flour and salt go in.
It's boiling now and I don't see any chunks of butter. How should I add the flour and salt without making a mess?
Lower the heat, then add the 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt together. Stir right away and keep the spoon moving so the mixture pulls together instead of clumping unevenly.
The mixture thickened fast and is pulling away in patches. Is that normal for this dough?
Yes, that's the right direction. Keep stirring vigorously until it leaves the sides of the pan and starts forming a stiff ball.
It's mostly one ball now, with a thin film on the pan. What should I check before I take it off the heat?

Check that the dough looks cohesive, stiff, and no longer loose or watery. Once it has pulled from the sides into a firm ball, take it off the stove and keep the greased cookie sheet ready for the next stage.
Can you walk me through Baked Apple Oatmeal while I get the oven and casserole dish ready?
Absolutely. Grease a 2-qt. casserole dish and set your oven to 350 degrees F so it can preheat while you start the oatmeal mixture on the stove.
The dish is greased. What ingredients should I put by the saucepan before I turn on the burner?
Set out 4 cups milk, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, 2 teaspoons butter or margarine, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and the cinnamon. Those are the items that get heated together in the saucepan.
I also have the oats nearby. Do they go in right away with the milk?
Not yet. Warm the milk, brown sugar, butter, salt, and cinnamon together first, stirring as the butter melts and the sugar dissolves.
The butter is melting and the milk looks warm around the edges. Should I bring it to a hard boil?
No hard boil is needed. Keep it gentle; once the mixture is hot and evenly combined, you can add the remaining ingredients.
Okay, the sugar looks dissolved. I have 2 cups old-fashioned oats ready. What do I do with them?
Add the 2 cups old-fashioned oats, along with any other remaining ingredients from your recipe, and mix gently so everything is moistened without mashing it up.
The oatmeal mixture is combined and still loose. Does that sound right before baking?
Yes, it can look loose at this point because the oats will absorb more liquid in the oven. Spoon the mixture into the greased 2-qt. casserole and spread it evenly.
It's in the casserole. Should it be covered before it goes in?
Yes. Cover the casserole, place it in the 350 degrees F oven, and bake it for 45 minutes.
After 45 minutes, what should I check before serving?
Look for oats that are tender and set, with the liquid absorbed rather than pooling at the edges. Let it sit briefly if it looks very loose, then serve warm.
Can you walk me through Country Fried Chicken while I set up the coating station?
Absolutely. Put a large resealable plastic bag on the counter for the dry coating and a shallow bowl nearby for the egg-and-milk mixture.
I've got the bag open. Which dry ingredients go in it?
Add 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika to the resealable bag.
Should I stir those in a bowl first, or is the bag enough?
The bag is fine. Seal it with some air inside and shake gently so the flour, garlic salt, pepper, and paprika are evenly mixed.
The dry mix looks even. What should I do with the shallow bowl?
Crack in the egg and add the milk, then beat them together in the shallow bowl until the mixture looks smooth and combined.
My chicken pieces are waiting on a plate. Do they all go in the bag at once?
Add the chicken a few pieces at a time so each piece has room to move. Seal the bag and shake until the pieces are coated with the flour mixture.
Some pieces have a light flour coating now. Do I go straight to the pan?
Not yet. Dip each coated piece into the egg-and-milk mixture, letting the excess drip back into the bowl.
After the egg dip, the coating looks wet and patchy. Is that expected?
Yes. Return those dipped pieces to the flour mixture in the bag and shake again so they pick up a second coating.
I'm trying to keep the counter from getting messy before serving. Any last setup advice?

Keep one plate for raw chicken and a separate clean plate or tray for the coated pieces. Once the chicken has been dipped in egg and shaken again in the flour mixture, it's ready for the next cooking or serving step your recipe calls for.
I'm making Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers and I've got my mixing bowl out. Can you walk me through what to gather first?
Set up the burger mixture ingredients near the bowl: 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, 1 small chopped onion, and 1 egg.
The cheeses, onion, and egg are on the counter. I also see ketchup and Worcestershire sauce in the instructions—do those go in the bowl too?
Yes. Add the ketchup and Worcestershire sauce with the cheese, onion, and egg, then season the mixture with salt and pepper.
Before I touch the beef, should I heat the grill or wait until the patties are shaped?
Go ahead and preheat the grill for high heat so it's ready when the patties are wrapped.
The grill is heating. How should the bowl mixture look before the beef goes in?

Stir it until the egg, cheeses, onion, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper are evenly combined. It does not need to be smooth; just make sure the seasonings are spread through the mixture.
Okay, the bowl looks evenly mixed. How do I add the ground beef without overworking it?
Crumble the ground beef into the bowl, then mix by hand just until the cheese-onion mixture is distributed through the meat. Stop once it holds together.
The meat mixture is combined. What size patties am I aiming for?
Divide the mixture into 6 patties. Try to keep them similar in thickness so they cook at the same pace on the grill.
I've shaped the patties. How do I handle the bacon so it stays on?
Wrap 1 slice of bacon around each patty. If the bacon wants to loosen, secure it with toothpicks before the patties go on the grill.
They're wrapped and the grill is hot. What timing should I use, and how do I know they're done?
Place the patties on the grill and cook for 5 minutes per side, or until well done. Remove any toothpicks before serving.
I'm making Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf and want to get my counter organized before I turn on the stove.
Start by preheating the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C. While it heats, put your skillet, slotted spoon, paper towels, and a baking dish or loaf pan within reach.
The oven is heating. Which ingredients should I chop and set beside the skillet?
Have 12 ounces of chopped raw bacon ready for the skillet. Also set out 1 small white onion, chopped, and 5 button mushrooms, chopped, since they'll go into the pan after the bacon fat is handled.
I've got the bacon, onion, and mushrooms ready. Should the beef stay cold for now?
Yes, keep the 1 1/2 pounds of extra-lean ground beef chilled until you're closer to mixing the meatloaf. For now, the stovetop work is about browning the bacon and preparing the onion and mushrooms.
My skillet is on the burner. What heat should I use for the bacon?
Use medium heat. Add the chopped raw bacon to the skillet and cook it until the pieces are browned, stirring so the pieces color evenly instead of sitting in one pile.
The bacon is sizzling and some pieces are browning faster than others.
Stir and spread the bacon out across the skillet. If the browned bits are getting too dark before the rest catches up, lower the heat slightly, but keep cooking until the bacon pieces are browned.
The bacon looks browned now. How do I move it without bringing along too much grease?
Lift the bacon out with a slotted spoon and transfer it to paper towels. Let the fat drain there while you deal with the grease left in the skillet.
There's a lot of bacon grease in the pan. How much should I leave for the vegetables?
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of bacon grease. That remaining tablespoon is enough to help cook the chopped onion and mushrooms without making the mixture overly greasy.
I left about 1 tablespoon in the skillet. Do the onion and mushrooms go in together?

Yes. Stir in the chopped white onion and the 5 chopped button mushrooms, then cook them in the bacon grease until they soften. After that, let the hot skillet mixture cool slightly before combining it with the 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef for the meatloaf.
I'm making Broccoli Cheese Crepes and want a calm walkthrough. What should I put on the counter first?
Start with the crepe batter items: 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Set a blender nearby, since the batter gets mixed there.
Got it. Should I measure the flour and salt before cracking the eggs?
Yes, that will make the blender step smoother. Measure the 6 tablespoons flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt into small bowls, then crack the 2 eggs and have the 1/4 cup water ready to pour.
The blender is out, and everything is measured. How do I start the batter?
Add the eggs, water, flour, and salt to the blender. Put the lid on securely before you blend so the batter stays contained.
How smooth should it be before I stop blending?
Process it until the batter looks smooth, with no obvious dry flour streaks. Once it reaches that point, let it stand for 15 minutes.
While the batter rests, what should I work on for the filling or sauce part?
Use that resting time to move to the small saucepan. Add the butter and onion, then sauté the onion until it turns tender.
What heat should I use for the onion so it softens without getting too dark?
Keep the saucepan at a controlled moderate heat and stir as needed. You're looking for tender onion rather than browning as the main cue.
The onion is soft now. What goes into the pan next?
Stir in flour until it's blended with the butter and onion. Keep stirring so the flour gets evenly moistened instead of sitting in dry clumps.
Before I start cooking the crepes, what should I check after the 15 minutes are up?

Give the rested batter a quick look: it should still be smooth and pourable. If it has settled a bit, gently stir it back together, then keep your pan and filling components close so assembly is easier.
Can you walk me through Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men? I'm setting up the mixing bowl and want to stay organized.

Start with the garlic so that handling stays in place: use 2 cloves, dice them finely, and set them near the balsamic vinegar. Then mince 1 celery stalk as small as you can so it blends cleanly.

It will work, but if it is very firm, let the 1/2 cup goat cheese sit for a few minutes while you measure the 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar. Softer cheese will blend into a smoother sauce.

Add the olive oil as the recipe directs, but go cautiously since there is no listed quantity. Put the goat cheese, minced celery, diced garlic, balsamic vinegar, and a small pour of olive oil in the bowl or blender cup, then blend and adjust texture only as needed.
That fits the way I like this sort of sauce; the same garlic move makes sense for Campagnard Sauce too.
Got it. Keep the garlic diced fine and let it meet the vinegar and oil rather than mixing it into the cheese by itself.
I'm adding everything to the blender cup now. Should salt and pepper go in before or after blending?
Add a small pinch of salt and pepper before blending, then taste after it turns smooth. Goat cheese can be salty, so hold back until you know what the sauce needs.
The blender is running, but I can still see tiny celery flecks. Is that a problem?
Tiny flecks are fine for Campagnard Sauce, but the base should look creamy and cohesive. Blend a little longer if you see separate bits of goat cheese or streaks of oil.
It's smoother now, kind of thick and tangy. Should I thin it more?
Only thin it if it is too stiff to spoon or spread. A small extra drizzle of olive oil can loosen it, but keep the balsamic vinegar at 2 tablespoons so the sauce does not get too sharp.
I tasted it and added a little pepper. Do I cover it right away?
Yes, scrape down the sides, cover the sauce, and refrigerate it. Chilling helps the goat cheese firm slightly and lets the garlic, celery, and balsamic settle together.
Before serving later, what should I check after it comes out of the fridge?
Stir it once, taste for salt and pepper, and check that it is smooth enough to spoon. If it tightened up in the refrigerator, loosen it with a very small drizzle of olive oil, then serve chilled.

Put 2 tablespoons butter or margarine near the saucepan, and measure 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour into a small dish so it can go in smoothly once the fat melts.

Measure it now: you'll need 1 3/4 cups water. Having it ready helps when you stir it in gradually after the flour is smooth.

Yes, use 1 (8 ounce) can tomato sauce for the enchilada-style sauce, along with the seasonings you're using, such as chili powder, bouillon, cumin, and salt.

Use moderate heat and melt the butter gently. You want it fully melted but not browned before the flour goes in.

Wrap the bacon snugly around each hot dog piece, but don't stretch it so hard that it tears. Once wrapped, push a toothpick through to hold it in place.

Let them cook on low for 5 to 6 hours, until the bacon is cooked. Before serving, make sure the bacon looks done and the toothpicks are still easy for people to notice or remove.

Roll each crepe snugly but gently, just enough to hold the banana and spread inside. Then place the rolled crepes in a warm skillet over medium heat.

Set out the 1 (5 pound) chuck roast, 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer. You'll also want a large bowl, cover for marinating, and a saucepan for the marinade later.
The sauces and beer are out. Do I mix everything straight into the bowl?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt until the marinade looks evenly mixed.
Should the chuck roast go in whole, or should I cut it up first?
Keep the roast whole for this recipe. Place it into the marinade, turn it so the surface is coated, then cover the bowl.
How long does it need in the fridge, and do I just leave it alone?
Refrigerate it for six hours, turning it often so the marinade keeps contacting different sides of the chuck roast.
When that time is almost up, what should I prep outside?
Preheat the outdoor grill for indirect heat, so the roast can cook without sitting directly over the flame.

Remove the roast from the marinade, then pour the marinade into a saucepan. Keep the raw-meat marinade handled separately until it's in the pan.

messages.content: I'm starting Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea, and the spice direction is the one part I'm not ready to lock in yet.

I've cleared the counter. What should I put by the stove before I turn on the heat?
Set a large pot on the stove, then bring over 1 pound fresh or frozen cranberries and 3 quarts cold water. A strainer will be useful later, but you do not need it right at the burner yet.
The cranberries are still frozen. Can I use them as they are, or should I thaw them first?
You can use fresh or frozen cranberries here. Put the cranberries and the cold water straight into the large pot, then make sure the pot has enough room for the liquid to boil without crowding.
They're in the pot with the water. How hard should I boil it?
Bring it up to a boil, then cook only until the berries pop, about 5 minutes. Keep an eye on the surface so it doesn't foam up or boil over.
I'm hearing some popping and the liquid is getting red. Do I keep going for the full time?
Use the popping berries as the main cue. If most of them have opened around that 5-minute mark, take the pot off the heat rather than boiling it longer.
The pot is off the burner. What happens during the long rest?
Let it stand at room temperature until cold, which will take several hours. That rest lets the cranberry liquid settle before you strain out the fruit.
While it cools, I want the rest measured so I'm not scrambling later.
Measure 2 cups orange juice and 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice. Also keep the lemon juice and sugar ready, since those get stirred into the strained cranberry liquid with the juices.
It's cold now, and I'm ready to strain and serve it neatly.

Strain out the cranberries, then stir the orange juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice, and sugar into the liquid. Once it tastes balanced and the sugar is dissolved, you can decide whether the first spice idea or the second one feels better for this batch.

Yes. Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt into separate small bowls or keep them ready nearby. That way you won't be scrambling once the butter and water are hot.
I've got the flour and salt measured. What size pan should I use for the butter and water?
Use a medium saucepan. Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to it before turning up the heat.
The butter and water are in the saucepan. How hot should I take it?
Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring as it heats. Keep stirring until the butter melts completely into the water.
The butter is mostly melted, but there are a couple little pieces still floating. Do I keep boiling?
Keep it at a boil just long enough for those last pieces to melt completely. Stir around the edges and bottom so the butter disperses evenly.
Everything looks melted now and the water-butter mixture is bubbling. Is that the texture I want before adding anything else?
Yes, the key check here is a full boil with the butter completely melted. You should see a uniform hot liquid rather than separate chunks of butter.

The recipe only calls for greasing the cookie sheet, so don't add flour or parchment unless you're choosing to use your usual pan setup outside the written directions.

Add the butter, vegetable oil, packed brown sugar, and white sugar to the large bowl together. Cream them until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.

Beat in the eggs and vanilla. Add them to the creamed mixture and mix until everything looks fully blended.

Check that the dough looks evenly mixed, with no dry streaks, and that your baking area is ready for portioning. Keep the oven at 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, while you prepare the cookies for baking.

Stir in the cheese, parsley, reserved chopped artichokes, and the sautéed onion-garlic mixture. Fold gently so the artichokes stay distributed through the batter instead of clumping in one spot.
